quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-01.prompt:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct subgroups of a finite group $G$. We say that $X$ and $Y$ are a *weird pair* if $|X| = |Y|$ and if no subgroup of $G$ other than $X$ and $Y$ has this same order.

(a) If $G$ is a group having a weird pair of subgroups, show that some subgroup of $G$ has a weird pair of normal subgroups.

(b) If $G = A \times B$ is a direct product of solvable groups, show that the subgroups $A \times 1$ and $1 \times B$ cannot be a weird pair.

(c) Show that a solvable group cannot contain a weird pair of subgroups.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-01.answer: (a) In $H=\langle X,Y\rangle$, conjugates of $X$ by $Y$ have order $|X|$ and are not $Y$, so $X,Y\trianglelefteq H$. (b) A nontrivial homomorphism $\theta\colon A\to A/N\cong C_p\hookrightarrow B$ gives a third subgroup $\{(a,\theta(a))\}$ of order $|A|$. (c) Reduce to $G=XY$ with $X,Y\trianglelefteq G$, pass to $G/(X\cap Y)=X/N\times Y/N$ and apply (b).

quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-02.prompt:
Let $R$ be a ring with $1$. Recall that an ideal $P$ of $R$ is said to be (right) *primitive* if there exists a simple right $R$-module $W$ with $P = \{r \in R \mid Wr = 0\}$. Furthermore, we recall that the Jacobson radical, $\mathrm{Jrad}(R)$, of $R$ is defined to be the intersection of all primitive ideals of $R$.

(a) Let $V$ be a right $R$-module having a composition series of length $n$ and suppose that $R$ acts faithfully on $V$. Show that $J = \mathrm{Jrad}(R)$ is an intersection of $n$ primitive ideals of $R$ and that $J^n = 0$.

(b) Give an example of the situation in part (a) with $n = 2$ and with $\mathrm{Jrad}(R) \neq 0$. Justify your answer.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-02.answer: (a) With composition factors $W_i=V_i/V_{i-1}$ and $P_i=\mathrm{ann}(W_i)$, $I=\bigcap P_i\supseteq J$ satisfies $V_iI\subseteq V_{i-1}$, so $VI^n=0$, $I^n=0$, hence $I\subseteq J$; so $J=I$ and $J^n=0$. (b) $R=\begin{pmatrix}K&K\\0&K\end{pmatrix}$ acting on row vectors $K^2$; $\begin{pmatrix}0&K\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ is a nonzero nilpotent ideal.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-03.prompt:
Let $f(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a monic polynomial with integer coefficients and suppose that $f(\alpha) = 0 = f(2\alpha)$ for some complex number $\alpha$.

(a) Show that $f(0)$, the constant term of $f$, is not equal to $1$.

(b) If $f$ is irreducible, prove that $\alpha = 0$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-03.answer: (a) If $f(0)=1$ then $\alpha\neq0$, and the product of the roots $\alpha\cdot2\alpha\cdot\prod\beta_i=\pm1$ makes $\tfrac12=\pm\alpha^2\prod\beta_i$ an algebraic integer, impossible. (b) Some $\sigma$ in the Galois group maps $\alpha\mapsto2\alpha$; then $\alpha=\sigma^m(\alpha)=2^m\alpha$, so $\alpha=0$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-04.prompt:
Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix over the complex numbers and let $A^*$ denote the conjugate transpose of $A$.

(a) Prove that all eigenvalues of the product matrix $A^*A$ are real and nonnegative.

(b) If $I$ is the $n \times n$ complex identity matrix, show that $\det(I + A^*A)$ is real and positive.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-04.answer: (a) If $A^*Av=\lambda v$, $v\ne0$, then $\lambda=\langle Av,Av\rangle/\langle v,v\rangle\ge0$. (b) The eigenvalues of $I+A^*A$ are $1+\lambda\ge1$, and the determinant is their product.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-05.prompt:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over some field $F$ and let $T\colon V \to V$ be a linear operator. Write $F[T]$ to denote the ring of all linear operators on $V$ that can be expressed as polynomials in $T$. Assume that no nonzero proper subspace of $V$ is mapped into itself by $T$.

(a) If $0 \neq S \in F[T]$, show that $\{v \in V \mid vS = 0\}$ is the zero subspace.

(b) Prove that $F[T]$ is a field.

(c) Show that $|F[T] : F| = \dim_F V$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-2001s-05.answer: (a) $\ker S$ is $T$-invariant (as $ST=TS$) and $\ne V$, so it is $0$. (b) Each $0\ne S\in F[T]$ is invertible and Cayley–Hamilton expresses $S^{-1}$ as a polynomial in $S$, hence in $T$. (c) $V$ is a vector space over the field $F[T]$ whose subspaces are $T$-invariant, so $\dim_{F[T]}V=1$ and $V\cong F[T]$ as $F$-spaces.
